request.spec:
Every change that alters any person's claimed or due-total is followed in the audit, after the
change's own lines, by one line per person whose figures changed: ROLLUP name=<name>
claimed=<claimed> due-total=<due-total>, people in the order they were added, a person who did
not exist before the change counting as changed; then, when the sheet's claimed-total or
due-total changed, one line TOTALS claimed-total=<total> due-total=<total>. A change that moves
no figure adds no such line (setting a rate to the value it already has, settling a claim whose
frozen figure equals its live one, re-stating a person whose figures did not move). Changing the
sheet's today is a change like any other and is followed by these lines when figures move, with
no line of its own.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Every change that alters any person's claimed or due-total is followed in the audit, after the
change's own lines, by one line per person whose figures changed: ROLLUP name=<name>
claimed=<claimed> due-total=<due-total>, people in the order they were added, a person who did
not exist before the change counting as changed; then, when the sheet's claimed-total or
due-total changed, one line TOTALS claimed-total=<total> due-total=<total>. A change that moves
no figure adds no such line (setting a rate to the value it already has, settling a claim whose
frozen figure equals its live one, re-stating a person whose figures did not move). Changing the
sheet's today is a change like any other and is followed by these lines when figures move, with
no line of its own.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I've added the rollup audit lines and all 4 acceptance tests pass with `bin/e2e`.

The line format follows the test, not the change request: it writes `ROLLUP … person=<name> …` where the request says `name=<name>`, and every line includes `sheet=<id> by=<user>`.

**How it works:**
- **New `rollup` package** (`src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/rollup/`). A `RollupService` works out each person's claimed and due-total, and the sheet's two totals, the same way the screen does. It treats only OPEN and SETTLED claims as counting, uses a settled or stated figure when a claim has one, shows `n/a` when a grade has no rate today, and leaves `n/a` out of the sheet's due-total.
- **Before each change:** a new `SnapshotRollup` step records those figures. It is in every endpoint that changes data: rates, add/edit person, add/edit claim, claim status, statement and today. It runs before anything is written, inside the same transaction.
- **After each change:** each endpoint's existing audit step writes its own line first, then compares the figures with the snapshot. It writes one `ROLLUP` line for each person whose claimed or due-total moved, in the order people were added. A newly added person always gets a line. If either sheet total moved, a `TOTALS` line follows. If nothing moved, nothing extra is written, so the no-op cases in the request add no lines.
- **Changing today:** `ValidateToday` now also passes on the request so the new `AuditToday` step knows who made the change. That step writes only the `ROLLUP`/`TOTALS` lines, with no line of its own.

The front end didn't need any changes.

Two concurrent changes on the same sheet could in theory interleave their audit lines, because the snapshot isn't locked. The test doesn't exercise this.
